name: Aspirin A10s hoax

card.summary: A 2023 social-media claim that very large aspirin intake could lighten brown eyes to blue, documented as an internet episode; eye colour itself is mainly genetic.
card.note: High-dose aspirin is toxic; no eye-colour effect has been documented.

quick.overview:
The Aspirin A10s claim began on X (formerly Twitter) around August 10, 2023, asserting that megadoses of aspirin inhibit iris melanin and turn brown eyes light blue. 'A10' refers to the lightest blue on a 1998 doll-catalogue eye colour chart that became a meme.[1]

It spread through posts, edited charts and ironic memes, and was quickly met with community notes and warnings about aspirin toxicity.[1] Eye colour is determined by iris melanin under polygenic control.[2]
quick.how: The claim was a meme, shared as posts and edited images; this wiki gives no dosing.
quick.risks: High-dose aspirin can cause ringing in the ears and, in overdose, serious toxicity with prolonged elimination.[3] No effect on iris colour is documented.

lead: The Aspirin A10s hoax was a short-lived social media claim, started on X on 10 August 2023, that taking very large amounts of aspirin could inhibit melanin and change brown eyes to light blue, 'A10s' being the top shade on a chart.[1] It is relevant to looksmaxxing because eye colour is a coveted trait and some users sought ways to change it.

The chart came from a 1998 My Twinn doll catalogue; it circulated online from about 2016 and was reworked in 2019 into an ironic hierarchy meme.[1] The hoax spread via viral posts and edited images and drew community notes warning of aspirin toxicity.[1]
Eye colour depends on iris melanin and is described as a polygenic trait.[2] Aspirin acts by irreversibly inhibiting cyclooxygenase, and at high doses may cause tinnitus and toxicity.[3]

angle.text: The claim proposed lightening brown eyes with aspirin. No documented mechanism or study shows this effect; the entry records the claim and its associated risks.

paras: The earliest posts showed eye photos with the claim that brown was 'receding', followed by an edited eye chart overlaid with aspirin amounts.[1]

Brown eyes have relatively high stromal melanin, and eye colour is polygenic.[2] Aspirin blocks prostaglandin production by acetylating COX; high doses can cause tinnitus, and overdose elimination is prolonged.[3]

timeline.event: Chart repurposed as an ironic hierarchy meme.[1]
Aspirin A10s claim appears on X.[1]

lore.intro: The claim circulated as a joke-and-earnest hybrid on X.[1]

claims.claim: Megadoses of aspirin turn brown eyes blue
claims.believers: Posters said aspirin inhibits melanin production in the iris.[1]
claims.experts: Eye colour is determined by genetics and iris melanin;[2] high-dose aspirin is associated with tinnitus and toxicity.[3] No studies show an iris colour effect.
